title: Lola Plants a Garden
author: Anna McQuinn

hero.name: Lola
hero.description: Young Black girl with natural hair, wearing overalls or gardening clothes, main character of the Lola series by Anna McQuinn
hero.source_note: Named series character — source from Creative Fabrica, TPT, or Anna McQuinn publisher resources; generic Boardmaker girl won't match the recognisable Lola character

ambiguous.issue: Could mean the noun (a plant/living thing) or the verb (to plant/dig in)
ambiguous.reason: In this book context a student is most likely to label the object they are growing; the verb sense is partially covered by core word 'go' and the action is shown in context with trowel and seed

notes: All 11 fringe words exist in the existing activity_images vocabulary for this book, so no new icons need sourcing beyond the Lola hero image. The board covers the core gardening narrative arc: preparation (gloves, trowel, pot), planting (seed, plant), care (watering can, sun), and nature rewards (bee, butterfly, flower, garden). 'Rake' and 'hose' from aac_extras are deprioritised in favour of words more central to Lola's specific story. If a secondary character such as Lola's mother appears prominently in classroom discussions, consider adding 'mum' as a swap-in for a less-used fringe word.

matching.note: Min 4 approved stems, no hard cap
